transcription: Verdicts and corrected fields copied verbatim from the verificador's final message; reasons condensed by the build session.

verdicts.reason: Verbatim on page 23; states the ISS tests ran in microgravity for normal and inverse flames, but it is a reproduced journal abstract: SECONDARY_SOURCE.

corrected.derivation: SECONDARY_SOURCE: the sentences come from the abstract of Kim et al., 'Spherical Gas-Fueled Cool Diffusion Flames', Proc. Combust. Inst. (2022), doi:10.1016/j.proci.2022.07.015, reproduced in section 4.C (p.23) of the Final Report. They cover both normal and inverse flames. Supporting report text on p.30: 'Testing is not conducted when thrusters fire or spacecraft dock or undock from ISS to ensure an acceptable acceleration environment.' Caveat on p.43: residual acceleration was 'not been evaluated with available measurements from the Space Acceleration Measurement System (SAMS)', and p.15 says SAMS data are not archived in PSI. Not used as gravity evidence: the project name and the PSI projectType label.

corrected.derivation: Same separate ground experiment as R2; not a CFI-G ISS test and not in the PSI tables. SECONDARY_SOURCE: the quote is from the reproduced abstract of Waddell et al., 'Cool Diffusion Flames in a Stably Stratified Stagnation Flow', Combustion and Flame, listed as 'submitted' (pp.23, 87). It is not the report's own statement and was not peer reviewed at the report date.

Domain trap: the inverse-flame 'XO2' up to 0.85 is the BURNER oxidizer stream; the chamber held fuel/N2 with no O2. Inverse row 21256 C2 says 'No nitrogen flowed. This repeats A3.', so its XO2 is probably planned, not delivered.
